newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK protesters demand China release Wang Dan.
newsitem.headline: HK protesters demand China release Wang Dan.

text.p: Demonstrators marched to China's unofficial diplomatic mission in Hong Kong on Tuesday to demand Beijing's release of Chinese dissident Wang Dan, who will go on trial on Wednesday.
"Release Wang Dan. Wang Dan is innocent," a group of about 50 protestors chanted as they marched through busy streets to the headquarters of Xinhua news agency, the de facto Chinese embassy here.
The protestors lit candles and staged a sit-down protest outside the Xinhua building. Organisers said some of their number would stay overnight.
Wang is charged with the capital crime of plotting to overthrow the government -- a crime that carries a maximum penalty of death and a minimum of 10 years in prison.

The 27-year-old activist has already served four years in jail for counter-revolutionary crimes, or subversion, for his role in pro-democracy demonstrations in Beijing's Tiananmen Square that were crushed by the army in June 1989 with heavy loss of life.

He had been active after his parole in 1993, defying persistent police surveillance to join in a daring appeal to communist leaders for the release of all those still in prison for their part in the 1989 protests.
Wang's mother said on Tuesday that she expected him to receive a harsh sentence.
"The court...giving my son a harsh sentence even though he is innocent is very likely to happen," Wang Lingyun told Reuters. "I dare not rule it out."
